data.name: Store development information
data.description: Stores development information provided in the request to make it available when viewing issues in Jira. Existing repository and entity data for the same ID will be replaced if the updateSequenceId of existing data is less than the incoming data. Submissions are performed asynchronously. Submitted data will eventually be available in Jira; most updates are available within a short period of time, but may take some time during peak load and/or maintenance times.
data.evaluateGuide:
Stores development information for Jira issues asynchronously, replacing older data for matching repository or entity IDs when the incoming update is newer.
Use for: submit build data, submit deployment data, update repository details, attach development data to issues
Not supported: reading development data, editing Jira issues, synchronous completion status

data.name: Submit Incident or Review data
data.description:
Update / insert Incident or Review data.
Incidents and reviews are identified by their ID, and existing Incident and Review data for the same ID will be replaced if it exists and the updateSequenceNumber of existing data is less than the incoming data.
Submissions are performed asynchronously. Submitted data will eventually be available in Jira; most updates are available within a short period of time, but may take some time during peak load and/or maintenance times. The getIncidentById or getReviewById o
data.evaluateGuide:
Creates or updates Jira incident and review data asynchronously, replacing older records when the incoming update sequence is newer.
Use for: submit an incident, update an incident, submit a review, update a review
Not supported: retrieving incidents or reviews, deleting operations data, synchronous completion status

data.name: Analyse Jira expression
data.description:
Analyses and validates Jira expressions.
As an experimental feature, this operation can also attempt to type-check the expressions.
Learn more about Jira expressions in the documentation.
Permissions required: None.
data.evaluateGuide:
Validates Jira expressions and can analyze their syntax and types. Use it to check whether an expression is well-formed before using it.
Use for: validate syntax, inspect expression errors, check expression types
Not supported: executing expressions, editing issues, retrieving issue data

data.name: Check issues against JQL
data.description:
Checks whether one or more issues would be returned by one or more JQL queries.
Permissions required: None, however, issues are only matched against JQL queries where the user has:

Browse projects project permission for the project that the issue is in.
If issue-level security is configured, issue-level security permission to view the issue.
data.evaluateGuide:
Checks whether specified Jira issues match one or more JQL queries, subject to the caller’s issue visibility permissions.
Use for: test issue filters, validate JQL matches, compare issues with queries
Not supported: searching full issue details, changing issues, returning inaccessible issues

data.name: Archive issue(s) by issue ID/key
data.description:
Enables admins to archive up to 1000 issues in a single request using issue ID/key, returning details of the issue(s) archived in the process and the errors encountered, if any.
Note that:

you can't archive subtasks directly, only through their parent issues
you can only archive issues from software, service management, and business projects

Permissions required: Jira admin or site admin: global permission
License required:
data.evaluateGuide:
Archives up to 1,000 Jira issues identified by issue ID or key and returns archive results and any errors. It requires administrator privileges.
Use for: archive issues by key, archive issues by ID, review archive errors
Not supported: archiving subtasks directly, restoring issues, archiving without admin access

data.name: Get Jira instance info
data.description:
Returns information about the Jira instance.
This operation can be accessed anonymously.
Permissions required: None.
data.evaluateGuide:
Returns information about the Jira instance, including its server details. It can be accessed anonymously.
Use for: identify Jira deployment, inspect instance details, check server information
Not supported: reading projects, changing configuration, managing issues

data.name: Archive issue(s) by JQL
data.description:
Enables admins to archive up to 100,000 issues in a single request using JQL, returning the URL to check the status of the submitted request.

data.evaluateGuide:
Archives up to 100,000 Jira issues selected by JQL and returns a URL for checking the asynchronous task status. It requires administrator privileges.
Use for: archive issues by JQL, bulk archive matching issues, review archive task status
Not supported: direct issue updates, restoring issues, archiving without admin access

data.name: Search issue IDs using JQL
data.description:
Searches for IDs of issues using JQL.
Use the Search endpoint if you need to fetch more than just issue IDs. The Search endpoint returns more information, but may take much longer to respond to requests. This is because it uses a different mechanism for ordering results than this endpoint and doesn't provide the total number of results for your query.
This operation can be accessed anonymously.

data.evaluateGuide:
Searches Jira with JQL and returns matching issue IDs only. Use the broader search endpoint when issue fields or complete issue details are needed.
Use for: find issue IDs, validate JQL results, identify matching issues
